section_1.title: Intuitive Hook: The Perspective Shift
section_1.content: Define 'Basis' as a coordinate system (a grid). Use an animation of a robot (Robby) standing in a 2D plane. Show that the same point in space can be described by different coordinate values depending on which grid (basis) Robby uses.
section_1.example: Robby the Robot: Position (2, 3) in a standard grid vs. position (1, 1) in a tilted, stretched grid.

section_2.title: Prerequisite Review: Basis and Linear Combinations
section_2.content: Quickly recap that any vector v can be expressed as a unique linear combination of basis vectors: v = c1*b1 + c2*b2. Use a visual 'Vector Summation' animation where two arrows (basis vectors) are stacked head-to-tail to reach a target point.
section_2.example: Representing vector v = [5, 7] as 5 times the unit vector 'i' plus 7 times the unit vector 'j'.

section_3.title: The Change of Basis Matrix (P)
section_3.content: Introduce the Transition Matrix P. Explain that P stores the old basis vectors expressed in terms of the new basis vectors as its columns. Provide the formula: [v]old = P * [v]new.
section_3.example: A transformation matrix P that converts coordinates from a 'Standard Grid' to a 'Camera View' for a character in a game engine.

section_4.title: Step-by-Step Computational Workflow
section_4.content: Demonstrate the algorithm: 1. Identify the new basis vectors. 2. Construct the matrix P. 3. Multiply P by the coordinate vector to get the new representation. Visual aid: Use color-coded columns to show how basis vectors map into the matrix.
section_4.example: Converting a coordinate from Basis B = { (1,0), (0,1) } to Basis B' = { (1,1), (-1,1) }.

section_5.title: Real-World Synthesis & Wrap-up
section_5.content: Conclude with an application: Why do we do this? It simplifies complex problems! Briefly show a physics simulation where changing the basis to align with an object's symmetry axis turns a difficult calculation into a simple diagonal matrix.
section_5.example: A spinning propeller: Changing the basis to align with the blade's rotation axis to simplify the force vector calculations.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Any vector is a linear combination.", "Summing basis vectors reaches any point.", "Coordinates are weights of the basis."]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Review: Basis and Linear Combinations", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define objects
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-1, 6], y_range=[-1, 6], axis_config={"include_tip": True}).scale(0.4)
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "E5")
        
        i_hat = Vector([1, 0], color="#F1C40F")
        j_hat = Vector([0, 1], color="#F1C40F")
        
        v = Vector([3, 2], color=WHITE)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#F1C40F"))
        self.play(Create(axes))
        self.play(GrowArrow(i_hat), GrowArrow(j_hat))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#F1C40F"))
        # Vector summation: v = 3*i + 2*j
        i1 = Vector([1, 0], color="#F1C40F").move_to(axes.c2p(0, 0), aligned_edge=LEFT)
        i2 = Vector([1, 0], color="#F1C40F").move_to(axes.c2p(1, 0), aligned_edge=LEFT)
        i3 = Vector([1, 0], color="#F1C40F").move_to(axes.c2p(2, 0), aligned_edge=LEFT)
        j1 = Vector([0, 1], color="#F1C40F").move_to(axes.c2p(3, 0), aligned_edge=DOWN)
        j2 = Vector([0, 1], color="#F1C40F").move_to(axes.c2p(3, 1), aligned_edge=DOWN)
        
        self.play(Create(i1), Create(i2), Create(i3), Create(j1), Create(j2))
        self.play(Create(v))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#2ECC71"))
        
        v_label = MathTex(r"v = 3\hat{i} + 2\hat{j}", color="#2ECC71").scale(0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(v_label, "A3")
        
        self.play(Write(v_label))
        self.wait(2)
